subtitle: Archaeogenetics, Archaeozoology, Historical Linguistics & Philology in the Indo-Iranian Sphere

events.title: Proto-Indo-European Expansion & Steppe Kurgan Culture
events.summary: Divergence of the Anatolian branch and formation of Core Indo-European within mobile pastoralist Kurgan cultures of the Eastern European steppe.

events.title: BMAC Oasis Civilization & Cultural Contact
events.summary: Monumental fortress and temple complexes in Central Asia. Provides the archaeological and linguistic substrate for ritual and agricultural loanwords in shared Indo-Iranian (e.g., soma/haoma).

events.title: Sintashta Chariots & Horse Domestication (DOM2)
events.summary: Oldest stratigraphically and radiometrically confirmed spoked-wheel war chariots. Modern domestic horses (Equus caballus, DOM2 lineage) expand from the Volga-Don region and correlate with the Indo-Iranian branch (R1a-Z93).

events.title: Arrival of Steppe Ancestry in Northwestern South Asia
events.site: Swat Valley (Katelai, Butkara) / Northwestern South Asia
events.summary: First detectable appearance of Steppe_MLBA in South Asia. Shows strong male-biased founder correlation (Y-haplogroup R1a-Z93/L657) and documents gene flow from Central Asia, whereas Mature Harappan genomes lack Steppe ancestry entirely.

events.title: Sinauli Cart Findings of the Copper Hoard Culture (OCP)
events.summary: Three burial chambers containing copper-sheathed two-wheeled vehicles, copper swords, and helmets. The debate over spoked versus solid disc wheels stands at the center of the controversy regarding autochthonous chariot development.

events.title: Desiccation of the Ghaggar-Hakra River System (Sarasvati)
events.summary: Climatic and hydrographic decoupling from glacial meltwater turns the perennial river into an ephemeral monsoon channel. Corresponds to the later Vedic depiction of the Sarasvati disappearing in the desert (Vinasana).

events.title: Mitanni Treaty: Earliest Indo-Aryan Linguistic Attestations
events.summary: King Šattiwaza of Mitanni swears by the Vedic deities Mi-it-ra, U-ru-wa-na, In-da-ra, and Na-sa-at-ti-ya. The Kikkuli horse-training manual preserves Old Indo-Aryan equestrian terminology (aika-wartanna) in the Near East.

events.title: Stratification and Composition of the Rigveda Text
events.summary: The older Family Books (II–VII) reflect the river geography of eastern Punjab and pastoral warrior traditions; the later books (I & X) document sedentarization in the Ganga Doab and increased Dravidian/Munda substrate influence.
